title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 749 customers reveals an overall churn rate of 37.7%. Monthly contract holders and an identified at-risk segment show significantly elevated churn. While churn rates are stable across signup cohorts and plans, Lifetime Value (LTV) scales dramatically with plan tier, offering a clear incentive for upgrades.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates are similar across plans, ranging from 36.6% to 38.9%. The Basic plan has the highest churn rate, followed by Standard and Premium.

Churn rates have remained relatively stable across signup cohorts, fluctuating between 36.7% and 39.8%. The 2024 cohort shows the highest churn rate at 39.8%, while the 2022 cohort was lowest at 36.7%.
Contract type is a strong predictor of churn. Monthly contract holders churn at 48.3%, which is 121.1% higher than the 21.9% rate for Annual contract holders.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers with high support tickets (≥5) and low satisfaction (≤2) exhibits a critical churn rate of 71.0%.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0) with a standard deviation of 13.2 months. Average satisfaction is 3.42, though 27 records are missing satisfaction scores.
Lifetime Value (LTV) increases significantly by plan. Premium LTV is $1,816.78, which is 292.0% higher than Basic LTV ($463.46). Standard LTV is $868.83.

limitations: Satisfaction scores are missing for 27 customers, potentially biasing the satisfaction mean.
The analysis is based on a snapshot and does not track churn over time.
Causal factors for churn were not modeled; reported associations do not imply causation.
conclusion: To reduce churn, prioritize converting monthly customers to annual contracts and intervene with the high-support, low-satisfaction segment. Upselling to Premium plans offers substantial LTV gains.
